item.description: SHARON TSAO WHO ARE ORIENTALS: MAGENTA REALISM July 3 – August 2, 2026 Second Saturday Reception: July 11, 5–8 PM About forty years ago, when I first came to California, I was told that I was “Oriental.” I was also told that certain tables and chests were “Oriental,” and that a particular decorative style was likewise considered “Oriental,” even though these things looked unfamiliar to me. item.title: Explore the Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument Region — Sat Jul 25, 2:00 PM — Mary L. Stephens – Davis Branch Library
item.description:
Learn more about this fascinating landscape, located just west and north of Davis in the northern Coast Ranges. Bob Schneider, coauthor of the recently published guidebook titled , Exploring the Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument Region, will share the wonders of this landscape, one shaped by ancient tectonic forces, uplifted ocean crust, and volcanic seamounts that have drawn the attention of geologists from around the world. Beyond its scientific significance, the monument offers rugged beauty, diverse wildlife habitats, scenic hiking opportunities, and traces of California’s rich mining heritage. The difficult history of our region’s diverse Indigenous Peoples in the area is told. Their new guidebook is well-illustrated, tells captivating stories, and provides detailed maps and route descriptions that allow you to explore the region on your own.
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Adrian West Band Live — Sat Jul 25, 8:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description: Adrian West Band is a rising force in the Bay Area music scene. Based in Oakland, the six-piece band plays original acoustic rock which they dub “Paul Simon meets Talking Heads”. A classically trained violinist who later turned to drums, guitar and singing, Adrian is a gifted composer and arranger. His lyrics, which range from whimsical to philosophical, ride atop a steady wave of catchy music. He always writes the music first and lyrics second, only adding lyrics if he feels the music stands tall on its own. Fun fact: Paul Simon and David Byrne (of Talking Heads) work pretty much the same way. Adrian figured out a while ago that he likes having trained jazz musicians in his band. Jazz musicians bring technical chops and versatility. They know how to listen to each other and make a song flourish. item.title: Watermelon Music Open Mic & Music Trivia — Sun Jul 26, 6:00 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
Come beat the heat and join us in the air-conditioned Melon Ball for the July Open Mic! We will continue to feature our Music Trivia contest throughout the evening in between acts. The winner will receive a $20 Watermelon Music gift card! Whether you’re looking for a venue to share your own talents or just looking to enjoy hearing (and seeing) some local performers, we invite you to this free monthly event. We provide the sound, stage and lights – the rest is up to you. Play us your favorite song, tell us some jokes, act out a scene from your favorite play with friends. item.title: Davis City Council Meetings — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis City Council provides policy direction, establishes goals, and sets priorities for City government. City Council holds regular meetings beginning at 6:30 p.m. on Tuesdays. Most commonly, meetings are held on the first and third Tuesdays of the month, with additional meetings scheduled as needed. The City Council meeting schedule is subject to change.
The Davis City Council meets in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. All regular meeting materials are posted at least 72 hours in advance and special meeting materials at least 24 hours in advance.
Visit the City Council site for information on agenda, special meetings, and more.
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.title: Human Relations Commission Meetings — Thu Oct 22, 6:30 PM — City Hall Community Chambers
item.description:
The Davis Human Relations Commission (HRC) meetings aim to promote mutual respect, understanding, justice, and advancing the human rights of all people. The Human Relations Commission meets on the fourth Thursday of each month at 6:30 p.m. The Commission takes a recess in July (no meeting in July).
Meetings take place in the Community Chambers at City Hall, 23 Russell Boulevard. For more information on meetings, membership, resolutions, and more, visit the Human Relations Commission site.
The HRC makes recommendations around equity and discrimination in the City, and supports the City in preventing and addressing discrimination while promoting diversity, equality, and justice relevant to the goals and policies of the City Council.
To contact or send emails to the commission, email: HRC@cityofdavis.org
Source: Hate-Free Together

item.description:
The Willow Snags (Sacramento, CA) are a rock band rooted in the blues and psychedelia of the 1960s. Typically found performing 2 – 3 hour sets in local haunts and dive bars in the Sacramento area, The Willow Snags had the honor of opening up for the legendary 4 Non Blondes at the Great American Music Hall on 12/17/2025. Featuring the talents of UC Davis alumni Mia Mercado on electric organ/vocals, UC Davis alumni Diego Martinez-Campos on percussion, Joshua Williams on lead guitar, Marisol Werner on rhythm guitar, and Johnny Mercado on vocals. $15 General Admission Concert starts at 8:00pm Doors open at 7:30pm This is a BYOB Event!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Jul 25, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Weekly Game Night at Blue Note — Wed Aug 12, 5:00 PM
item.description:
Yolo County Board Game Gathering Update 8/14/25: **We're still active**, but we primarily use Discord to chat and plan events. (See group description for invite link.)
We still meet every Wednesday for board games at Blue Note Brewing Company. We'll have a handful of tables reserved near the back; just look for the pile of board games.
People usually start arriving around 5pm, and games start whenever people are ready. Blue Note closes at 9pm, and although we have a 5-10 minute grace period there, you should be in the process of final scoring by 9, or else pack it up and play again another day.
Game night is open to all ages! Blue Note is a brewery, not a bar, so there's no restriction against minors. In addition to their crafted-in-house beer selection, water and sodas are available.

item.description:
The beloved Picnic in the Park season is back at the Davis Farmers Market starting Wednesday, April 1, 2026! Every Wednesday evening through August 26, the market expands to 4:00 – 8:00 PM, turning Central Park into the perfect spot for a relaxed picnic dinner. Shop fresh produce, artisan goods, and a wide variety of prepared foods from your favorite vendors. Enjoy local craft beer, wine, and brand new this year – mead! Each week features live music and children’s activities, creating a festive, family-friendly atmosphere. Bring blankets, lawn chairs, and reusable bags. It’s the ideal way to unwind, connect with neighbors, and support local farmers and food makers. This year is extra special as the Davis Farmers Market celebrates its 50th Anniversary!
